![](../../src/images/hex_complex.png){.intro_image} This is our final style guide for this course to help you develop a consistent syntax for creating communicable, readable code! Well-formatted code is not just an end product though -- recommendations in this document will help you explore and debug your code *as you write it*. Moreover, a portion of your grade will be based on adhering to this style guide (up to 10% per problem set)! Style guides, such as this one, are common across many computer languages and organizations. Although "style" represents a preference (i.e., it does not influence code output), using a style guide does make collaboration easier! Herein, I borrow heavily from the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/){target="_blank"}, from which most of the formatting rules below were derived. I include only elements from the tidyverse style guide that are relevant to the content in this course and have included additional or modified elements that, in my opinion, provide added utility or enhanced code readability. This lesson provides all the code formatting rules that we will follow in this course. I suggest returning to this *often* and comparing your problem set answers with this guide prior to submission. I provide a description of the code formatting rules, examples of each, and any exceptions to the rules. *Note: I have often gotten the question of whether my own code uses our course style guide -- it does not. My personal style guide is much more strict! The course style guide is greatly simplified to make it easy to adhere to.* The “Additions” section, below, only includes new formatting rules that were not present in Lesson 2.5: Course style guide, part 2. The “Style guide” section is a comprehensive list of all our formatting rules thus far.
:::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - Now that you have gotten the hang of pipes, we are loosening the **nested functions** rule -- you may now nest functions **three** levels deep! *Note: Although there will be instances where you will need to nest functions three levels deep, you should still try to use pipes whenever possible!* :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mean( as.numeric( factor( c("boy", "howdy") ) ) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c("boy", "howdy") %>% factor() %>% as.numeric() %>% mean() ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - If a function is on the same line as another function, and the number of arguments across functions is three or more, place each argument of the parent function on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} summarize(mean(howdy, na.rm = TRUE), .by = boy) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} summarize( mean(howdy, na.rm = TRUE), .by = boy ) ``` ::: :::: - If a filtering operation (`filter()`) has more than one logical test, place each test on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} filter(boy < 3, howdy == "hello") ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} filter( boy < 3, howdy == "hello" ) ``` ::: :::: - If a newly assigned column requires more than one line to create (given the rules above), add a new line after `=`. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mutate( boy = c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} mutate( boy = c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ) ) ``` ::: :::: ::: ## Style guide ### Horizontal spacing :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Commas** should be followed by one trailing space, but not a leading space. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c(1,1 , 2, 3 , 5) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5) ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: More than one space *can* be added after a comma if it improves the alignment within a code block. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel ```{r} tribble( ~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` *Note: Also see "square brackets" section, below.* ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Infix functions** (e.g., `%in%`, `+`, `<-`, `=`): Should be separated from surrounding code with a single leading and trailing space. ::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} country<-c("boy", "howdy") nerdy <-c("hello", "world") formal<- c("warm", "wishes") my_list <- list( country= "boy howdy", nerdy ="hello world", formal= "warm wishes" ) 1/2 1+ 2 1 ==2 c(11, 23, 32)%>% mean() ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} country <- c("boy", "howdy") nerdy <- c("hello", "world") formal <- c("warm", "wishes") my_list <- list( country = "boy howdy", nerdy = "hello world", formal = "warm wishes") 1 / 2 1 + 2 1 == 2 c(11, 23, 32) %>% mean() ``` ::: ::: - **Exception**: The extraction (`$`) and colon (`:`, `::`) infix operators should not be preceded or followed by a space. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} my_list$ nerdy my_list $nerdy readr ::read_csv readr:: read_csv 1 :4 1: 4 ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} my_list$nerdy readr::read_csv 1:4 ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: You can add more than one space before or after the = operator if it improves code block alignment. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel ```{r} sayings <- tibble( country = c("boy", "howdy"), nerdy = c("hello", "world"), formal = c("warm", "wishes") ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Prefix** **functions** (e.g., `c()`, `tibble()`): Should not be followed by a space. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c ("boy", "howdy") ! TRUE ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c("boy", "howdy") !TRUE ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: Include a trailing space after \~ if it is used as a prefix function. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c(1, 2) %>% map_dbl(~1 + .x) tribble( ~x, ~y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c(1, 2) %>% map_dbl(~ 1 + .x) tribble( ~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Parentheses** (...):  - Opening and closing parentheses should not be preceded by a space. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c ("boy", "howdy") c("boy", "howdy" ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c("boy", "howdy") ``` ::: :::: - If the opening parentheses and function arguments are on the same line, the opening parentheses should not be followed by a space. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c( "boy", "howdy") ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c("boy", "howdy") ``` ::: :::: - If the opening parentheses and the first argument of a function are on different lines, the first argument should be indented two spaces (one tab stop) relative to the start of the line above. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c( "boy", "howdy" ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c( "boy", "howdy" ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Square brackets** (subsetting `[...]` and extraction `[[...]]` operators) Should not be preceded or followed by a space. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} my_list [[1]] my_list[ 1] ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} my_list[[1]] my_list[1] ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: When subsetting or extracting a multi-dimensional object inside of square brackets (e.g., `df[1, ]`), include a single space for rows or columns in which all data are returned. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} sayings[, -1] sayings[1,] ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} sayings[ , 1] sayings[1, ] ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Nested functions** should be indented *two* spaces (one tab stop) relative to the parent function. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mean( c(11, 23, 32) ) mean( c(11, 23, 32) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} mean( c(11, 23, 32) ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Pipe operators** (%\>%): The line following the first pipe in a piped code block should be indented two spaces (one tab stop) relative to the line above. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c(11, 23, 32) %>% as.integer() %>% typeof() c(11, 23, 32) %>% as.integer() %>% typeof() ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c(11, 23, 32) %>% as.integer() %>% typeof() ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Comments**: Add a single space between the hashtag (#) and comment. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} #my section header -------------------------------------------- #My atomic vector: c(1, 2) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} # my section header ------------------------------------------- # My atomic vector: c(1, 2) ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Vertical spacing :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Code blocks**: Maintain *one* blank line between code blocks. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c(1, 2) list(1, 2) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c(1, 2) list(1, 2) ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: Do not separate adjacent `library()` functions with a blank line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel ```{r} library(lobstr) library(tidyverse) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Comments**: Maintain *one* blank line between code blocks and comments. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} # my section header ------------------------------------------- # My atomic vector: c(1, 2) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} # my section header ------------------------------------------- # My atomic vector: c(1, 2) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Code and comments**: Should not be on the same line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} rm(sayings) # Remove object from the global environment ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} # Remove object from the global environment: rm(sayings) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Code within a single code block**: Should not be separated by blank lines unless it is separated by a comment. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5) %>% factor() ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5) %>% factor() c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5) %>% # Convert to a factor: factor() ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Line breaks :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Code and comments** should not exceed 80 characters in width (if it is avoidable) -- add a line break, if possible. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} brood_x_cicadas <- c("Magicicada cassini", "Magicicada septendecim", "Magicicada septendecula") ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} brood_x_cicadas <- c( "Magicicada cassini", "Magicicada septendecim", "Magicicada septendecula" ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Prefix functions**: Include no more than *one* prefix function per line of code. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} typeof(as.numeric(1:4)) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} typeof( as.numeric(1:4) ) ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: Prefix operators, infix operators, and functions used to calculate summary statistics of a data object (e.g., `mean()`, `n()`, and `length()`). :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel ```{r} select(!howdy) sum(boy$howdy) summarize(n = n()) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Arguments in a function**:  :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - If you provide three or more arguments to a function, place each argument on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c("roger", "pete", "john", "keith") ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ) ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: When using the `c()` or `list()` functions, you may include up to five numeric values. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel ```{r} c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5) ``` ::: :::: ::: - If a function is on the same line as another function, and the number of arguments across functions is three or more, place each argument of the parent function on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} summarize(mean(howdy, na.rm = TRUE), .by = boy) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} summarize( mean(howdy, na.rm = TRUE), .by = boy ) ``` ::: :::: - If you have more than one `=` in a function, place each argument on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} ggplot() + aes(x = boy, y = howdy) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} ggplot() + aes( x = boy, y = howdy ) ``` ::: :::: - If a filtering operation (`filter()`) has more than one logical test, place each test on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} filter(boy < 3, howdy == "hello") ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} filter( boy < 3, howdy == "hello" ) ``` ::: :::: - If a newly assigned column requires more than one line to create (given the rules above), add a new line after `=`. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mutate( boy = c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} mutate( boy = c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ) ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Parentheses for functions that span more than one line**: - Opening parentheses should be followed by a line break. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} tribble(~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} tribble( ~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` ::: :::: - Closing parentheses should be placed on their own line and indented to the same level as the start of the function. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mean( c(1, 1)) tribble( ~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} mean( c(1, 1) ) tribble( ~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Assignment**: If a code block spans more than one line of code, add a new line after the assignment operator . :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} my_list <- list( country = "boy howdy", nerdy = "hello world", formal = "warm wishes" ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} my_list <- list( country = "boy howdy", nerdy = "hello world", formal = "warm wishes" ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Pipe operators** (`%>%` or `%>%`): Code that follows a pipe operator should be placed on a new line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} list(1, 2) %>% str() ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} list(1, 2) %>% str() ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Assignment :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Global assignment**: Always use the `<-` operator for global assignment. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} my_vector = c(1, 2) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} my_vector <- c(1, 2) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Assigned names**: Global assignments and variable names should be written in snake_case. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} my.phrases boyHowdy HelloWorld list( boyHowdy = 1, HelloWorld = 2 ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} my_phrases boy_howdy hello_world list( boy_howdy = 1, hello_world = 2 ) ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Functions :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Nested functions** should not be nested deeper than **three** levels (use a pipe instead!). :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mean( as.numeric( factor( c("boy", "howdy") ) ) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c("boy", "howdy") %>% factor() %>% as.numeric() %>% mean() ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Logicals**: Spell out `TRUE` and `FALSE` in a function's argument. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mean( c(1, NA, 3), na.rm = T ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} mean( c(1, NA, 3), na.rm = TRUE ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Named arguments**: If you modify the default behavior of a function's argument, include the name of the argument. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} factor( c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ), c( "keith", "john", "pete", "roger" ) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} factor( c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ), levels = c( "keith", "john", "pete", "roger" ) ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Named functions**: Always provide parentheses when running named/non-operator prefix functions. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} ls search ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} ls() search() ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Other :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Negated selection**: Avoid using `-` for negated selection. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} select(-howdy) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} select(!howdy) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Single quotes**: Avoid using single quotes when referring to character values -- only use them when necessary (see **Preliminary lesson 2: Values**). :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c('boy', 'howdy') ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c("boy", "howdy") ``` ::: :::: ::: ```{=html} ```

**Exception**: When subsetting or extracting a multi-dimensional object inside of square brackets (e.g., `df[1, ]`), include a single space for rows or columns in which all data are returned. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} sayings[, -1] sayings[1,] ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} sayings[ , 1] sayings[1, ] ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Nested functions** should be indented *two* spaces (one tab stop) relative to the parent function. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mean( c(11, 23, 32) ) mean( c(11, 23, 32) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} mean( c(11, 23, 32) ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Pipe operators** (%\>%): The line following the first pipe in a piped code block should be indented two spaces (one tab stop) relative to the line above. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c(11, 23, 32) %>% as.integer() %>% typeof() c(11, 23, 32) %>% as.integer() %>% typeof() ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c(11, 23, 32) %>% as.integer() %>% typeof() ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Comments**: Add a single space between the hashtag (#) and comment. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} #my section header -------------------------------------------- #My atomic vector: c(1, 2) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} # my section header ------------------------------------------- # My atomic vector: c(1, 2) ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Vertical spacing :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Code blocks**: Maintain *one* blank line between code blocks. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c(1, 2) list(1, 2) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c(1, 2) list(1, 2) ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: Do not separate adjacent `library()` functions with a blank line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel ```{r} library(lobstr) library(tidyverse) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Comments**: Maintain *one* blank line between code blocks and comments. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} # my section header ------------------------------------------- # My atomic vector: c(1, 2) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} # my section header ------------------------------------------- # My atomic vector: c(1, 2) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Code and comments**: Should not be on the same line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} rm(sayings) # Remove object from the global environment ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} # Remove object from the global environment: rm(sayings) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Code within a single code block**: Should not be separated by blank lines unless it is separated by a comment. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5) %>% factor() ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5) %>% factor() c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5) %>% # Convert to a factor: factor() ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Line breaks :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Code and comments** should not exceed 80 characters in width (if it is avoidable) -- add a line break, if possible. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} brood_x_cicadas <- c("Magicicada cassini", "Magicicada septendecim", "Magicicada septendecula") ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} brood_x_cicadas <- c( "Magicicada cassini", "Magicicada septendecim", "Magicicada septendecula" ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Prefix functions**: Include no more than *one* prefix function per line of code. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} typeof(as.numeric(1:4)) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} typeof( as.numeric(1:4) ) ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: Prefix operators, infix operators, and functions used to calculate summary statistics of a data object (e.g., `mean()`, `n()`, and `length()`). :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel ```{r} select(!howdy) sum(boy$howdy) summarize(n = n()) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Arguments in a function**:  :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - If you provide three or more arguments to a function, place each argument on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c("roger", "pete", "john", "keith") ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ) ``` ::: :::: - **Exception**: When using the `c()` or `list()` functions, you may include up to five numeric values. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel ```{r} c(1, 1, 2, 3, 5) ``` ::: :::: ::: - If a function is on the same line as another function, and the number of arguments across functions is three or more, place each argument of the parent function on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} summarize(mean(howdy, na.rm = TRUE), .by = boy) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} summarize( mean(howdy, na.rm = TRUE), .by = boy ) ``` ::: :::: - If you have more than one `=` in a function, place each argument on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} ggplot() + aes(x = boy, y = howdy) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} ggplot() + aes( x = boy, y = howdy ) ``` ::: :::: - If a filtering operation (`filter()`) has more than one logical test, place each test on its own line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} filter(boy < 3, howdy == "hello") ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} filter( boy < 3, howdy == "hello" ) ``` ::: :::: - If a newly assigned column requires more than one line to create (given the rules above), add a new line after `=`. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mutate( boy = c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} mutate( boy = c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ) ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Parentheses for functions that span more than one line**: - Opening parentheses should be followed by a line break. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} tribble(~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} tribble( ~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` ::: :::: - Closing parentheses should be placed on their own line and indented to the same level as the start of the function. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mean( c(1, 1)) tribble( ~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} mean( c(1, 1) ) tribble( ~ x, ~ y, 11, 2, 3, 5 ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Assignment**: If a code block spans more than one line of code, add a new line after the assignment operator . :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} my_list <- list( country = "boy howdy", nerdy = "hello world", formal = "warm wishes" ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} my_list <- list( country = "boy howdy", nerdy = "hello world", formal = "warm wishes" ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Pipe operators** (`%>%` or `%>%`): Code that follows a pipe operator should be placed on a new line. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} list(1, 2) %>% str() ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} list(1, 2) %>% str() ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Assignment :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Global assignment**: Always use the `<-` operator for global assignment. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} my_vector = c(1, 2) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} my_vector <- c(1, 2) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Assigned names**: Global assignments and variable names should be written in snake_case. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} my.phrases boyHowdy HelloWorld list( boyHowdy = 1, HelloWorld = 2 ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} my_phrases boy_howdy hello_world list( boy_howdy = 1, hello_world = 2 ) ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Functions :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Nested functions** should not be nested deeper than **three** levels (use a pipe instead!). :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mean( as.numeric( factor( c("boy", "howdy") ) ) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c("boy", "howdy") %>% factor() %>% as.numeric() %>% mean() ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Logicals**: Spell out `TRUE` and `FALSE` in a function's argument. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} mean( c(1, NA, 3), na.rm = T ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} mean( c(1, NA, 3), na.rm = TRUE ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Named arguments**: If you modify the default behavior of a function's argument, include the name of the argument. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} factor( c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ), c( "keith", "john", "pete", "roger" ) ) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} factor( c( "roger", "pete", "john", "keith" ), levels = c( "keith", "john", "pete", "roger" ) ) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:0em;"} - **Named functions**: Always provide parentheses when running named/non-operator prefix functions. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} ls search ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} ls() search() ``` ::: :::: ::: ### Other :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Negated selection**: Avoid using `-` for negated selection. :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} select(-howdy) ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} select(!howdy) ``` ::: :::: ::: :::{style="margin-bottom:-2em;"} - **Single quotes**: Avoid using single quotes when referring to character values -- only use them when necessary (see **Preliminary lesson 2: Values**). :::: indent_code_bb ::: panel [Bad:]{.bad} ```{r} c('boy', 'howdy') ``` [Good:]{.good} ```{r} c("boy", "howdy") ``` ::: :::: ::: ```{=html} ```
